title: A rational toric rule with resolving centered monoscheme lifts
statement: There exists a rule F assigning a finite normalized blowup tower to the rational realization of every fine torsion-free monoscheme with finite affine cover, including finite disjoint unions, together with its smooth-scheme contracted-pullback comparisons and identity/composition equations [lem-trf-monoscheme-tower-comparison-coherence]. There is a centered lift rule T for F: its saturated monoscheme towers have the same ordered stages, actual monoid ideals realizing the ring ideals, canonical realization identifications, fine torsion-free intermediate objects, and unique centered local isomorphisms compatible with those identifications. Its transported ring centers are torus invariant. For each input M the terminal monoscheme of T(M) is smooth. This assertion does not supply comparisons between the monoscheme towers, or any fan tower.

source.place: Expose VIII, construction 3.2.19 (first half) and Theorem 3.2.20, p.106.

proof.text: Fix one smooth-functorial normalized rational toric desingularization rule from [lem-trf-toric-normalized-desingularization]. Forget its extra action fields to obtain the SchemeRule of [lem-trf-monoscheme-tower-comparison-coherence], keeping the towers, smooth-scheme comparisons and identity/composition equations. Keep its terminal regularity and invariant nowhere-dense centers for the next step.

For each input apply [lem-trf-monoscheme-toric-tower-descent] to the assigned tower. Keep its ordered tower, base identification, torsion-freeness, realization isomorphisms, arrows and exact centers to form a Lift. The regular endpoint and the last clause of tower descent give terminal smoothness. For any other Lift, compare inductively starting with the pinned base. Injectivity in [lem-trf-toric-monoid-comparison] identifies the centers under the preceding local isomorphism. The identical saturated blowup fraction charts give local isomorphisms at the next level, unique because they fix every fraction over the previous level; [lem-trf-normalized-blowup-calculus] identifies their realizations with the prescribed normalized scheme maps. This produces a LiftIso, and the same induction proves its uniqueness. The toric charts transport the original invariant ideals, giving LiftRule.invariant. No contraction or comparison of two different input towers is asserted here.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_resolvingLiftRule :
    ∃ F : SchemeRule.{u}, ∃ T : LiftRule F,
      ∀ M : Input.{u},
        ((T.lift M).tower.level (Fin.last (F.tower M).length)).IsSmooth
